title: ProRL: Prolonged Reinforcement Learning Expands Reasoning Boundaries in Large Language Models
location: Sec. 4 intro (p. 6); Fig. 10 IFEval panel (p. 21); Fig. 3
quote: and re-run all other benchmarks: math, code, STEM reasoning, and instruction following
measures: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B (distilled start) vs an intermediate and the final ProRL checkpoint, 256 samples, aggregate IFEval pass@k to k=256 (read from Fig. 10: k=1 0.443 vs 0.659; k=128 0.859 vs 0.886); IFEval checker; no per-prompt split
reason: Closest prior large-k start-vs-RL comparison on an IF benchmark, but aggregate only, IFEval (close to its RL IF data), 1.5B distilled start; net gap ~3 pts at k=128, far below our ~20% per-prompt RL-only share on IFBench

title: VerIF: Verification Engineering for Reinforcement Learning in Instruction Following
quote: a high pass@k at large k suggests untapped potential that RL can exploit
measures: TULU 3 SFT and R1-Distill-Qwen-7B (start models only) on IFEval, pass@k to k=64, prompt-level strict; pass@64 > pass@1 by >20 points; no RL-model large-k comparison
reason: Large-k IF measurement of start models only, used to motivate RL as sharpening of latent ability; no start-vs-RL boundary or per-prompt reach

title: Generalizing Verifiable Instruction Following
quote: IF-RLVR increases a Qwen-2.5-7B base model to scores of 87.8 (IFEval) and 54.7
measures: IF-RLVR (GRPO) from Tulu-3-8B-DPO and Qwen2.5/Llama/OLMo base and instruct starts; pass@1 on IFEval and IFBench (58 unseen constraints); no pass@k, no per-prompt reach
reason: Establishes large pass@1 IF-RLVR gains including on constraint types absent from training, but never asks whether the gains lie inside the start's large-k support

title: Olmo 3
quote: with the final RL training stage leading to the biggest improvements in Olmo 3’s precise instruction-following abilities
measures: Same model family: Olmo 3 Think 32B SFT / DPO / RL(3) / RL(3.1) pass@1: IFBench 37 / 34.4 / 47.6 / 68.1, IFEval 83.7 / 82.3 / 89.0 / 93.8; pass@K only for AIME (SFT vs DPO, K<=32)
reason: Replicates only our pass@1 direction (DPO 34.4 to 68.1 vs our 0.290 to 0.683 strict); no large-k or per-prompt IF analysis

title: Where does output diversity collapse in post-training?
quote: We study 13 Olmo 3 checkpoints at the 7B scale.
measures: Olmo 3 7B Think-SFT / Think-DPO / Think(RL) on IFEval, K=16 at T=0.6: strict@1 (greedy) 78.0 / 74.9 / 78.7, pass@16 90.9 / 86.7 / 91.7, aggregate; main topic is output diversity
reason: Only prior Olmo 3 Think DPO-vs-RL IF comparison at k>1 found: 7B, IFEval, k=16, aggregate; no reach or RL-only prompts

title: Does RL Expand the Capability Boundary of LLM Agents? A PASS@(k,T) Analysis
quote: RL expands the capability boundary by 5 problems with only 1 regression (net +4)
measures: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct vs its GRPO agent on HotPotQA bridge and comparison QA with a retrieval tool (100 test problems each), PASS@(k,T) to k=64, per-problem: 5 RL-only vs 1 base-only on each; MATH-500 control 3 vs 3; exact-match grader
reason: A non-maths per-prompt RL-only share has been reported (~5% at k=64, no fresh-draw confirmation, tool-use QA, instruct start); much smaller than our ~20% and not IF

title: What Outcome RL Buys: Finishing, Reliability, Rarely Reach
quote: Reach adds at most 2.1 percentage points on any of our four physics and math sets.
measures: 20 released RL models (1.5B-32B) vs their thinking-model starts on physics and maths; reach = RL-only minus start-only at k=8 (k=32 appendix); 144 RL-only physics items resampled or read, 3.5% hold up
reason: Supports the maths/physics contrast class (reach rare) with the same confirm-on-fresh-draws logic as ours; says nothing about IF

title: Mitigating Exploration Bias in RL for Multi-Instruction Following
quote: the policy model’s initial ability to satisfy hard instructions is too low to trigger successful exploration during RL training
measures: Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct GRPO-trained on IFTrain 3-5-constraint prompts; per-instruction-type pass rates before vs after RL and training-time instruction coverage per rollout group; IFBench/IFEval pass@1; no large-k reach
reason: Argues RL neglects instructions the start rarely satisfies (a support-limit view in tension with our RL-only prompts) but measures no large-k boundary

title: What Outcome RL Buys: Finishing, Reliability, Rarely Reach
quote: Where the base often hits the token budget before answering, most of the change, gain or loss, is finishing (82% at 4k and 8k).
measures: 20 RL-vs-start pairs (1.5B-32B) on physics and competition maths at fixed token budgets; pass@1 change split into finishing / reliability / reach
reason: Prior evidence that truncation of the start under the token budget carries most apparent RL gain (maths/physics, pass@1); our OMEGA case (start cut off on 255/256 at RL's 32k cap) is a reach-level instance

title: When Pass@k Crossovers Are Real - and Why: Paired Inference and the Markov Kernel of RLVR
quote: per-response token limits alone can create, mask, or reverse a crossover through asymmetric truncation
measures: Nine public RLVR checkpoints vs their starts (e.g. DeepScaleR-1.5B vs R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B) on maths at 3k-32k token limits, pass@k with paired confidence bands; start truncation 30.6% vs 12.2% at 8k
reason: Shows the start-vs-RL large-k comparison depends on asymmetric truncation at the token limit (maths); same caveat as our OMEGA cap finding

title: Generalizing Verifiable Instruction Following
quote: the IF-RLVR trained models tend to generate shorter reponses, with an average token length of 210.
measures: Average IFBench response length: frontier models 2,214 tokens vs IF-RLVR-trained models 210 tokens; descriptive only
reason: Notes IF-RLVR models answer far shorter, but does not tie brevity to which prompts RL newly solves

title: When Built-in Thinking Helps and Hurts: Constraint-Level Error Shifts in Instruction Following
measures: Qwen3 1.7B-32B on IFEval, same weights Thinking ON vs OFF; 10-20% of prompts flip pass/fail; matched-length analyses substantially reduce the Precision-class drop
reason: Final-answer length confounds per-prompt IF pass/fail differences, but between modes of one model, not RL vs start, and no large k

title: What Outcome RL Buys: Finishing, Reliability, Rarely Reach
quote: Given more tokens, the base closes most of the finishing gap itself.
measures: Starts re-read at budgets above RL's cap; 144 RL-only physics problems resampled or read (3.5% hold up); maths/physics, k=8
reason: Prior test of our C8 logic (give the start more tokens; resample or read RL-only items) on maths/physics; budget explains most gains there vs 1 of 3 OMEGA prompts for us; no IF or prompt-hint test

title: When Pass@k Crossovers Are Real - and Why: Paired Inference and the Markov Kernel of RLVR
quote: Re-evaluating public RLVR checkpoints exposes per-response token limits as a major truncation confound
measures: Same checkpoints re-evaluated at 8k / 16k / 32k: verdict on the DeepScaleR crossover changes with the limit (none / unsupported / supported)
reason: Raising the token limit changes start-vs-RL verdicts (maths); our 65k re-run is the same control applied to RL-only prompts

title: GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning
quote: for IFBench, GEPA found optimal prompts after just 678 rollouts achieving 38.61%, outperforming GRPO’s test set score of 35.88% with 24,000 rollouts.
measures: Qwen3-8B on IFBench and five other tasks: reflective prompt optimisation vs GRPO (LoRA, 24k rollouts), aggregate pass@1: baseline 36.90, GRPO 35.88, GEPA 38.61
reason: A prompt change matches or beats RL on IFBench in aggregate (RL gave no gain there); no per-prompt elicitation of RL-only prompts, no large k

title: ProRL: Prolonged Reinforcement Learning Expands Reasoning Boundaries in Large Language Models
quote: We compare the base model (DeepSeek-R1-Distilled-1.5B), an intermediate checkpoint
measures: Pass@k to k=256 on IFEval and other tasks for the start, an intermediate and the final ProRL checkpoint; on IFEval the intermediate sits at the start's level (ProRL added IF data only from its third training run), aggregate only
reason: Uses an intermediate RL checkpoint on large-k IF curves (aggregate), as our step-750 test does per prompt; no comparable early-reach finding
